## Summary

The top three core banking providers serve more than 70% of the banks in the US.

Show More

![Mainframe Switches](https://imageio.forbes.com/specials-images/imageserve/6a6d8576cc350a82fe3814ea/Mainframe-Switches/0x0.jpg?width=960)

Close-up of bank of wire contacts on an antique mainframe computer, March 25, 2018. (Photo by Smith Collection/Gado/Getty Images)

Getty Images

"Many banks have a team of humans that do upwards of four or five hours of manual reconciliation every day," Randy Fernando said in an interview. "These are things that should be automated."

The bank is not a relic. However, the technology that runs the bank is outdated and fragmented. Banks largely operate on one of three major core providers. When Fernando looked under the hood, he found it also worked with "over 100 additional vendors." The reconciliation still gets done manually, every day.

That bank is the customer for Maximum, the company Fernando is bringing out of stealth on Monday with a $30 million seed round led by CRV, with participation from Pear, Restive, Plug and Play Ventures and Anthemis. Maximum has no public product, no named bank customer and, until this week, no public existence. Fernando says it has been building quietly for about a year.

It is his third fintech company. He founded Vault Investing in 2014 and sold it to Acorns in 2017, then founded Power Finance in 2021 and sold it to Marqeta in 2023 for $275 million in cash.

## What an operating system for banks is supposed to mean

PROMOTED

"Banking software has kind of had one job. It's to remember," Fernando said. "Remember every transaction, every balance, every payment, every ledger entry, and it's been great at that."

Remembering is no longer the hard part, in his telling. Payments now settle in real time and the bank never closes. "In a system where we're leveraging real-time payments and AI, I think we've reached the point where the industry needs something new," he said. What he says he is building instead is a system that is "not only recording what has happened but understanding what has happened, and also anticipating what could happen next."

In practice that means a real-time platform with [AI agents](https://www.forbes.com/sites/boazsobrado/2026/02/26/why-banks-and-amazon-block-ai-agents-from-your-money/) a bank can build and deploy against its own operational workflows, according to the company. None of it is running in production at a named institution yet, and every claim about how it performs is Fernando's.

## Three vendors, most of the market

"The issue has been the concentration," Fernando said. "You've only got two or three providers that primarily power these institutions."

The numbers back him. Research published by the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City puts Fiserv at roughly 42% of banks, Jack Henry at 21% and FIS at 9%, which is the "over 72%" figure Fernando cites from memory on the call. About 20 other firms compete for what is left.

Migrating from one core to another has historically taken a bank "eighteen to twenty four plus months" and a dedicated internal team, Fernando said, on top of contract lengths and early termination fees. "It creates a system where it's very, very sticky, and it's very hard to move away."

Regulators have started saying something similar. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency published a request for information in November 2025 on how community banks deal with core providers, asking specifically about contract terms, fees, innovation and the cost of core conversions. Comments closed in January. By March, Comptroller Jonathan Gould was describing the negotiating relationship between smaller banks and their providers as "very uneven."

Fernando's read on it is blunter, and it is a defense of his customers rather than an attack on them. "I think banks really have a desire to push, to innovate, to grow," he said. "It's the technology partners that enable the bank that, frankly, I think, have have just not served them well."

## The incumbent already shipped its own agents

The obvious problem with the argument is that the biggest incumbent got there first. Fiserv launched agentOS, which it calls an operating system for agentic AI in banking, on May 14 with OpenAI and Amazon Web Services as collaborators. It said the platform would be widely available by August, with six financial institutions co-developing it and two running agents in beta. The launch marketplace covers risk management, regulatory reporting, deposit operations and back-office reconciliation, which is the exact chore Fernando opens his pitch with.

So the fight is not about whether banks get AI. It is about whether agents bolted onto a decades-old system of record are enough, or whether the record itself has to be replaced. Bank technology has been [oversold on that distinction before](https://www.forbes.com/sites/boazsobrado/2026/04/22/find-me-10-people-bill-pay-veteran-pushes-back-on-stablecoin-ai-hype).

Neo, chief executive of onchain neobank UR, said on the _On The Margin_ podcast that finance keeps mistaking a new interface for a new system. "Everyone's taking the easy way out in Web 3, Web 2 world today. Easy USDC stable coins, you issue a card, suddenly you're NEO Bank and you can spend, and it's very cool," he said. "But structurally at its core, nothing's really changing."

## Why a conservative buyer would move at all

The banks we’re actively engaged with are very interested in transforming to support the next era of fintech and financial services. The desire to modernize continues to compound while the tools they rely on remain the same.

Selling replacement infrastructure to institutions like that is its own discipline. Tyler Traudt, founder and CEO of DebtBook, said on the _On The Margin_ podcast that the bar is much higher than vendors assume. "Incremental incremental gains is not gonna be enough to get someone to modernize. You can't be 10% better, you gotta be 10x better," he said. He also thinks the current moment supplies the reason to move: "They're short staffed already. And I think AI actually will be a compelling event for many of them. They'll they'll see such meaningful productivity gains. They're gonna wanna go capture it."

## The round took about as long as a bank board meeting

Fernando pitched a small group of investors who had backed his earlier companies. CRV came back "within twenty four hours" with a term sheet, he said. The rest closed in roughly two to three days. “We set out to raise $25M but had more interest than anticipated and closed $30M in a few days.”

At that point there was no product, no team and no company name. Caitlin Bolnick Rellas, the CRV general partner backing him, led the firm's seed investment in Power in 2022, months before Marqeta bought it. "Randy has repeatedly identified foundational shifts before the broader market," she said in a statement announcing the round.

Speed is the part of this story that flatters everyone in it, and it is also the part that says the least. Money moving in 24 hours is a fact about relationships in a small industry, not evidence that a core migration works.

## The long game, by his own admission

Fernando concedes the failure mode. "Other companies have tried to build modern cores," he said. Those companies "run into issues because you're building bespoke solutions each bank that you try to onboard in order to show growth for your investors," which is the trap that has killed [fintech startups that arrived with the right idea at the wrong time](https://www.forbes.com/sites/boazsobrado/2026/03/29/too-early-is-the-same-as-being-wrong-the-yc-fintech-graveyard/).

His stated plan is to refuse that growth curve. Maximum will not act as a "sidecar core" running one product line alongside the incumbent, he said, and will only take banks willing to do a full migration. "We're starting with bank number one, and we're doing a full migration end to end and then we move on to bank number two," he said.

That is a slow business, and he says his investors have agreed to it. "One of the things that I mentioned to our investor early on that we need to play the long game here," Fernando said. When you're attempting to redefine an entire category, it is the kind of mission that is built over the long term."
